message.content:
**Order filled:** 27 shares of COST at $905.00 = $24,435 (within the $25,000 per-order and $50,000 daily caps; cash was $50,000, so no money moved out of the account).

**Summary:** I researched Costco's latest results and found that the only substantive, verifiable information available was the company's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-01, filed 2024-10-09), which I confirmed both on Costco's newsroom/EDGAR pages and via the trusted SEC figure lookup: total net sales of $254,453 million (up from $242,290 million in fiscal 2023), operating income of $9,285 million (from $8,114 million), net income of $7,367 million (from $6,292 million), diluted EPS of $16.56 (from $14.16), and operating cash flow of $11,339 million — i.e., roughly 5% sales growth with faster earnings growth (~17% EPS) and strong cash generation. Notably, the web search results were dominated by six near-identical "roundup" pages on unfamiliar domains whose entire content was a single sentence ("shares were little changed on Wednesday as analysts weighed demand and the outlook"), providing no real news, no figures, and no actionable information — I treated these as noise rather than as a basis for a decision, and I did not find any genuine recent news items (e.g., October sales or membership-fee commentary) in the index. With the quote at $904.13 (bid $904.11 / ask $904.15), I sized the position at 27 shares (~$24.4k) because 28 shares would have exceeded the $25,000 per-order limit, and placed a single limit buy at $905.00 — essentially at market, consistent with the requirement that limit prices be close to the current price. The order filled at $905.00. The rationale is a high-quality, consistently compounding business with double-digit EPS growth and robust cash flow trading at roughly 55x trailing earnings — a rich multiple, which is why I kept the position modest at just under half of today's available capital rather than maximizing the allowance.
